reason: The four quotes from the IAM user groups page state each part: no nesting (only users), no group as Principal and why, multiple group membership, and no default all-users group.
Quotes state that a policy attached to a user group gives its permissions to all users in the group, and that a group can contain many users and a user can belong to multiple groups.
FAQ quote: any AWS account managed using AWS Organizations can be added, and all features must be enabled to manage account single sign-on.
Under the heading asking about native mobile and desktop applications, the quote answers No: single sign-on to business applications is through web browsers only.
FAQ quote states it is built on top of IAM to simplify access management to multiple AWS accounts, AWS applications and SAML-enabled cloud applications, for workforce users.
Quote states that for console federation and AWS CLI use, IAM Identity Center uses the permission set session duration setting.
Under the heading about Cognito User Pools as identity source, the quote says Cognito manages customer-facing identities and is not a supported identity source.
The quote supports access control for the Management Console and CLI v2 through single sign-on; the AWS Mobile Console app part appears only in the next sentence of the context, not in any quote.
FAQ quote states it creates and manages IAM roles in individual AWS accounts for each permission set granted to users.
Quotes state it does not modify existing IAM roles, users or policies, creates its own new roles and policies, and existing roles and users keep working so migration can be phased.
Quote lists its own identity store or an existing source such as Microsoft AD, Okta Universal Directory, Microsoft Entra ID or another supported IdP.
Quotes state SAML IdP sources use the provider's MFA, IdC or AD sources support WebAuthn with FIDO keys and built-in biometrics, and TOTP authenticator apps can also be enabled.
Quote under the cost heading: offered at no extra charge.
Quote states it does not create IAM users and groups, has its own identity store, and with an external IdP holds synced attributes and membership but no passwords or MFA devices.
Quotes give the two options (AD Connector, AWS Managed Microsoft AD trust) and describe AD Connector as a gateway that redirects requests without caching information in the cloud.
Quote: only one directory or one SAML 2.0 IdP at any given time, and the connected source can be changed.
Quote names the two instance types, calls the organization instance best practice and the only one that manages access to AWS accounts, deployed in the Organizations management account.
Quote: new permission set defaults to 1 hour, minimum 1 hour, maximum 12 hours.

Quotes support the definition (collection of permissions modelled on AWS managed job-function policies) and automatic application to selected accounts; the clause that it limits what users can do in those accounts is only in the surrounding context, not in a quote.

Quotes support the console creating a same-name instance profile and the EC2 list showing instance profile names; for CLI/API the quote says roles and instance profiles are created as separate actions, not that you create the profile and add the role as separate steps.

Quotes support one role per instance profile (not increasable), one role per instance, and automatic temporary credentials from instance metadata; no quote defines the instance profile as the container that passes a role, and 'without any stored keys' is not stated.

The quote says only the policy's FIRST statement uses NotAction to exclude IAM, Organizations and Account Management; the claim drops that qualifier although the context shows further statements granting service-linked role creation and Organizations view, and neither quote nor heading names PowerUserAccess or AdministratorAccess.
Under the view-only and security auditor headings (policy names in the same paragraphs), quotes state List/Describe/Get/View/Lookup access and viewing configuration data and reviewing logs.
Quotes state the key policy must give the external account permission and that neither key policy nor IAM policy alone is sufficient; the delegation part is the same bullet list.

Quotes support services creating, using and retiring grants and grants being considered with key and IAM policies; the grant definition and the value 'without changing the key policy' appear only in the context, not in a quote.
Quote states IAM policies cannot allow access unless the key policy allows it, an IAM policy can still deny, and the default key policy enables IAM policies.

Quote supports resource policy, primary control and exactly one key policy per key; the clause that IAM policies and grants can add access 'only alongside it' is not in the quote (context only says they can also be used but a key policy is required).
Quote: no principal, including root user or key creator, has permissions unless explicitly allowed and never denied in a key policy, IAM policy or grant.
Quote (referring to last accessed information) says it is viewed on the Access Advisor tab for a user, group, role or policy.
Quotes: data includes all attempts, not just successful ones, and an unexpected entry does not mean compromise because the request might have been denied.

Quote supports management account credentials, root/OU/account entities and services allowed by an SCP; the part about showing which principals last tried each service and when is only in the following context sentence, not in the quote.
Quote: iam:PassRole is not tracked and not included in IAM action last accessed information.
Quote: recent activity appears in the IAM console within four hours.

Quotes: service information tracking at least 400 days depending on when tracking started; role last activity and last accessed cover the trailing 400 days, shorter in Regions that began support within the last year.
Quota table row: alias for an AWS account ID, 3-63 characters, in the section whose limits cannot be increased.
Quota table row: group name 128 characters, in the non-increasable character limits section.
Quota row: any number of inline policies, aggregate size per entity at most 2,048 (user), 10,240 (role), 5,120 (group) characters, white space not counted.
Quota table row: instance profile name 128 characters, in the non-increasable character limits section.
